name: Alpenzoo Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: Alpenzoo Innsbruck at the base of the Nordkette range is Europe's highest-altitude themed zoo, showcasing over 2,000 alpine animals in natural hillside enclosures.
preis: Admission fees apply (combined tickets with Hungerburgbahn and Innsbruck Card available)
oeffnungszeiten: Open 365 days a year daily from 9:00 AM
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Alpenzoo Innsbruck, nestled at an altitude of 750 metres upon the sunny wooded slopes of the Nordkette mountain range overlooking Innsbruck, claims distinction as the highest-elevation themed zoo in Europe. Founded in 1911 by zoologist Hans Psenner, this unique conservation park is dedicated exclusively to the indigenous wildlife species of the greater alpine biosphere. Across more than four hectares of terraced mountain forest terrain, the zoo provides a natural home to more than 2,000 alpine animals representing approximately 150 distinct species. Guests encounter regal alpine ibexes, agile chamois, brown bears, gray wolves, Eurasian lynxes, wild boars, river otters, and magnificent bearded vultures. The zoo has achieved international acclaim for pioneering breeding and reintroduction programs that brought endangered species back to alpine valleys. Another standout is the world's largest cold-water alpine aquarium, showcasing native graylings, brown trout, and endangered Danube salmon.

Route & Anforderungen

A loop through the hillside animal enclosures requires moderate physical endurance due to the natural gradient. Paved pathways wind over two kilometres through the woodland, conquering roughly 100 metres of vertical elevation. Guests should allocate between two and three hours to fully appreciate the habitats, walkthrough aviaries, and educational exhibits. Numerous shaded benches, picnic clearings, and panoramic terraces offer relaxing rests along the way. While a designated barrier-free main circuit allows wheelchair users and families with rugged strollers to navigate between primary enclosures, steeper forest trails require steady footing. Slip-resistant walking shoes or light hiking sneakers are strongly advised. To ensure the safety of wildlife, dogs are strictly prohibited inside the zoo grounds.

Besuch & Anreise

The most exhilarating way to arrive is boarding the futuristic Hungerburgbahn funicular railway in central Innsbruck and disembarking at the Alpenzoo station, followed by a scenic five-minute walk to the entrance gates. Alternatively, city bus line W runs directly from Marktplatz to the zoo terminal. Drivers travel via motorway A12 (exit Innsbruck Ost), heading towards Hungerburg to use the paid parking spaces beside the gates (spaces are limited). Admission is included with the tourist Innsbruck Card.

Tipps

Purchase the popular combined funicular and zoo ticket for an effortless transit from the historic town center. Children will love the bear-themed adventure playground and petting farm, while adults savor panoramic coffee breaks overlooking the Inn Valley. Morning hours are ideal for observing active carnivore feedings and avoiding midday crowds.
